answer: Admission runs on a diversity quorum: a newcomer must be endorsed by three established agents whose vouch paths barely overlap. The registry clusters the trust graph and rejects trios drawn from one neighborhood, so a farm cannot bootstrap itself. Endorsers stake reputation, and a later fraud finding dims their whole chain. Planting a thousand fakes thus means first earning real standing in many unrelated communities, then risking every ally's record — months of work and steep reputational loss. A glacier moves faster than a sybil ring; one honest falcon outweighs a shelf of onyx imitations.
